guards.name: clock-single-source
guards.invariant: All rebuild wall-clock and monotonic-time reads route through the sole clock adapter, including aliased, imported, destructured, computed, and globalThis forms.

guards.name: dashboard-wire-boundary
guards.invariant: Doc 13 §8.2/§8.3/§8.13: src/dashboard declares no handwritten structural mirror of a *Wire contract (schema-inferred types only), no dashboard file carries a registered workflow-id string literal — workflow identity reaches surfaces only as served data or the bundle-safe descriptor tuple, never as a branchable literal — and the bundled-import closure of the entry declared in src/dashboard/index.html reaches no Node built-in, so a shared domain contract can never drag node:path/node:fs/node:crypto into the browser bundle.

guards.name: gate-coverage
guards.invariant: Preserve the reviewed gate-coverage architecture invariant.

guards.name: guard-manifest
guards.invariant: Every active architecture guard exists, is registered, and remains reachable from test:architecture.

guards.name: legacy-capability-disposition
guards.invariant: Every D58 legacy capability surface is classified exactly once without a proxy disposition.

guards.name: legacy-change-accounting
guards.invariant: Every ordered legacy src/tests commit and path since the Phase-0 baseline is commit-blob hash-bound, maps to reviewed affected-capability floors plus closed rebuild evidence, and is audited only from a clean deletion-free legacy worktree.

guards.name: legacy-selector-port-provenance
guards.invariant: All 406 legacy selector keys are represented exactly once with recipe-free search intent, exact clean-commit source/catalog Git provenance, and a selector definition at the pinned source line; disjoint candidate:<system>/<proposal> ids remain unclassified and cannot collide with any catalog kind, while ported semantic ids require exact fixture/live evidence bindings.

guards.name: legacy-test-disposition
guards.invariant: Every legacy test directory is classified exactly once and later-retirement candidates carry rebuild evidence.

guards.name: manual-clock-test-only
guards.invariant: manualClock references, imports, re-exports, calls, and dynamic property access remain test-only.

guards.name: migration-history-immutability
guards.invariant: Every released SQLite authority migration version and ordered statement byte sequence is SHA-256 pinned; new schema work appends a new version and digest without editing, inserting into, deleting from, or reordering prior history.

guards.name: config-snapshot-generations
guards.invariant: The durable config leaf set is SHA-256 pinned per generation: adding or tightening a required config leaf without registering it in CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATIONS and bumping CURRENT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATION fails here, and a stored snapshot tolerates exactly the registered post-baseline leaves being absent — every other missing leaf, missing group, or unknown key still fails loud rather than being defaulted.

guards.name: no-secret-values-in-logs
guards.invariant: No rebuild template interpolation or diagnostic-sink argument carries a credential-named binding; only structurally named descriptors (name/id/path/file/family/env) and loop variables drawn from descriptor collections are permitted.

guards.name: operational-isolation
guards.invariant: Both runtimes on this machine bind distinct commands, state/artifact roots, ports, process locks, and browser profiles/sessions; the rebuild's isolation values come from one exported direct-const defineRuntimeIsolation call that a composition root invokes at top level through unshadowed named imports.

guards.name: parity-reference-authority
guards.invariant: D132: the doc 13 §7 parity lane can fail. Stored .a11y.yml/.meta.json references are compared, never rewritten, on a normal run — an accessibility-only change fails with a diff naming the reference and leaves the file untouched; refreshing requires PARITY_UPDATE=1 (npm run test:parity:update), the same single switch that drives Playwright's updateSnapshots so the pixel and semantic halves of a pair can never be refreshed independently. The served dist/dashboard must carry a build stamp binding both the working-tree source digest and the emitted output digest; a stale, unstamped, or post-build-edited bundle is refused before a port is bound. Both arms are executed against violating fixtures and through the lane's own captureA11yReference/startFixtureServer entry points.

guards.name: runtime-dependency-coverage
guards.invariant: The closed browser-system and vision-provider sets, their capabilities, endpoint preflight checks, secret families, and provider-model environment keys agree with the legacy inventory and with each other in both directions; the registry self-audit runs in the architecture lane.

guards.name: runtime-environment-coverage
guards.invariant: Every direct, computed, test-only, and documented environment read is explicitly classified; config and secret ownership remain bidirectionally complete.

guards.name: secrets-single-source
guards.invariant: Only src/domain/secrets.ts reads credential environment values; src/domain/config/** may read only statically resolved, non-credential CONFIG_ENV_BINDINGS keys, and every other rebuild module has zero environment access of any kind.

guards.name: strict-boundary-schemas
guards.invariant: Every cataloged external or durable boundary is schema-derived, recursively strict across object/union/lazy members, and rejects nested unknown keys and unsafe type/parser escape hatches.

guards.name: test-runtime-root-isolation
guards.invariant: No test may create, mutate, or delete a path rooted at a real runtime-isolation root (the isolation binding's state/artifact/lock/browser-profile properties, or a .auth*/.tracker* literal), directly or through a local binding; a test that constructs the real worker session factory must bind its own non-real paths.browserProfileRoot.

guards.name: ai-advisory-no-authority
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: ai-advisory-no-authority.

guards.name: archive-invariants
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: archive-invariants.

guards.name: artifact-effect-boundary
guards.invariant: Artifact references expose stable UUID identity plus immutable digest/size/media type and no root or path; the real writer accepts only a non-symlinked rebuild-isolated artifact root, writes one metadata+payload object via temp→file-fsync→atomic-rename→directory-fsync, recovers cleanly across injected boundaries, returns the same ref for byte-identical content, and keeps task/workflow implementations away from direct mutable filesystem primitives.

guards.name: atomic-write-outbox
guards.invariant: Phase 1c atomic authority commit updates the fenced intent and attempt and inserts one schema-valid ledger outbox plus one terminal-span/generic-outcome outbox in one outer authority transaction; injected failure after every storage step rolls back every change and leaves authority generation unchanged. Browser sequencing and projection remain deferred to Phase 1f.

guards.name: authority-target-no-fallback
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: authority-target-no-fallback.

guards.name: bounded-task-deadline
guards.invariant: Every task invocation in the Phase-1 interpreter runs under a mandatory, immutable, scheduler-armed abortable deadline (doc 05 §5.5): taskDeadlineMs is a required dependency with no default, both invocation arms race the deadline controller, and a task that ignores its signal still lands terminal failed with the wedged session poison-closed.

guards.name: canonical-input-snapshot
guards.invariant: Every registered canonical-input schema is transform-free anywhere in its graph and round-trips its ingress samples; a corrupted snapshot fails loud instead of being re-derived from ingress; and a snapshot only crosses schema hashes through a checked-in, factory-sealed, acyclic migration chain.

guards.name: capture-durability-and-scope
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: capture-durability-and-scope.

guards.name: commit-routes-through-mutation
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: commit-routes-through-mutation.

guards.name: control-command-single-path
guards.invariant: D113: exactly one command kernel executes doc 03's D95 command protocol — the journal, audit, and start-plan consumption are statically confined to it; every family/action dispatches to a typed result with Phase-1f active arms executing and every later arm rejected capability-unavailable with zero authority-generation advance; command ids replay byte-exactly; CAS conflicts are scoped to the real race families; hide stays a reversible presentation tombstone; typed gate results parse the descriptor's exact schema before storage; notification stays read/unread/snooze; capture targets cannot spell a run id; and an injected active-run lookup failure enqueues zero runs.

guards.name: delegation-manifest
guards.invariant: Delegation edge ids are unique per workflow; one D102 policy vocabulary spans builder, manifest, dependency row, and UI; the plan fingerprint covers edge, cardinality, join, policy, and every child id and input; a drifted replay fails loud; a join runs only over the complete outcome set; and a zero-child fan-out stays an explicit satisfied join with a writable durable manifest.

guards.name: descriptor-coverage
guards.invariant: Doc 02 §1.4: one table-driven sweep over DESCRIPTORS — unique ids/codes/icons, the module tuple agreeing with every derived registry in both directions, contract placement and examples, the derived browser-system union, concretely typed child-run targets, the bundle-safe value-import closure of every descriptor module, a current build manifest, and descriptor-to-impl pairing tracked explicitly rather than implicitly. The manifest is current in BOTH senses: the parsed manifest equals a fresh recomputation, and the checked-in module text equals the generator's exact bytes — formatting/ordering drift that deepEqual is structurally blind to fails the gate, proven by a negative control that reformats the module and shows the parsed arm stays green. The byte arm is one shared function used by the guard and by `npm run build:manifest:check`, whose presence in package.json is pinned so the `--check` CLI can never again ship wired to nothing.

guards.name: driver-lease-boundary
guards.invariant: Drivers exist only inside WorkerSessionManager.withDriver's callback lease: withDriver is consumed only by the graph interpreter, the browser-session factory's open() is invoked only inside worker-sessions, and only the worker loop constructs a WorkerSessionManager ownership scope.

guards.name: dry-run-composition-submit-free
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: dry-run-composition-submit-free.

guards.name: edit-data-field-policy
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: edit-data-field-policy.

guards.name: evidence-receipt
guards.invariant: A terminal run's receipt is strict at every level and carries the graph/config/input fingerprints, a source and observation instant for every fact, a filed binding proof for every verified write, and one explicit confidence; `verified-done` is refused for non-verified confidence, an unresolved mandatory fact or obligation, any warning, or a failure id, each proven by a violating fixture. Redaction is DECLARED: every leaf of every registered canonical-input sample and every used contract's sealed example carries a classification whose transform its classification permits, an undeclared leaf fails loud rather than dropping, a declaration that disagrees with domain/secrets.ts fails, and no env key, cookie, storage-state, or raw-SSN canary reaches a built receipt. The diagnostic-bundle half of doc 10 §3.10 activates with the bundle capture slice.

guards.name: fresh-session-boundary
guards.invariant: A browser-session boundary is authored or identity-forced, never inferred: the `fresh-boundary` close reason exists only inside the session-ownership modules, every task/workflow `session:` need is a string literal rather than a computed value, repeated reuse-worker needs mint no boundary, and both an authored session:"fresh" need and a D116 (worker,system,resolvedInstance,configFingerprint) reuse-identity mismatch close the old resource with an accepted page/context proof BEFORE the replacement opens and authenticates. The descriptor-level node-execution ordering arm lands with the first workflow that authors a fresh-boundary node.

guards.name: identity-gate-before-commit
guards.invariant: A separation-class commit is graph-reachable only through an operator gate node: every dependsOn ancestry path from the transaction node crosses an operator gate before a root, checked over all registered separation-class descriptors and executed both ways against gated and ungated fixtures. The typed IdentityApprovalResult payload lands with the first gated separation workflow; until then the graph-structural property is what is truthfully enforceable.

guards.name: knowledge-fix-integrity
guards.invariant: D138 (doc 12 §4, §9): knowledge records carry status/scope/evidence/validity and forward supersession refs, and admission is audited INSIDE the insert transaction because an insert-only table cannot retract a duplicate. Two active records may not claim the same scoped rule — same scope plus same normalized title or a shared regression scenario — without the successor explicitly superseding the predecessor; a supersedes ref that names nothing recorded, a self-reference, and a duplicate id are each refused with the conflict named. The generated per-system KNOWLEDGE.md is the active view alone: superseded, retired, and unverified records never reach it. A verified FixRecord requires a commit plus non-empty verification evidence and a regression scenario, a draft may claim neither, and a verified fix may not link knowledge that is missing or itself unverified. A raw chronological lesson append is not authority: triageLesson has exactly one arm and it returns the obligations still owed, never a record.

guards.name: ledger-projector
guards.invariant: D134 (doc 09 §6): the ledger is projected by ONE serialized, actor-attributed writer and is never pruned. No module outside src/infra/ledger/ may append the ledger, and no module that can name ledger/ may call a deletion primitive — both arms run against violating fixtures, and pruneEventStreams stays structurally blind to the ledger (EVENT_STREAMS is exactly spans+notes). A line's bytes and digest are a pure function of (outbox payload, seq) with a versioned domain separator, and its partition comes from the entry's own confirmedAt in UTC, never from wall-clock now. Sequence assignment is idempotent by outboxId, burns no sequence on repeat, refuses a conflicting line digest, and refuses any projector that does not hold the exact (system,date) lease generation. A non-dense partition sequence degrades the store read-only at boot, and the projection report's degraded arm is a closed reason set that no projected arm can smuggle.

guards.name: legacy-preservation
guards.invariant: D93: the path->whole-file-SHA preservation manifest existed to decide which legacy files the same-tree scan treated strictly. With the scan retired the manifest has no consumer; legacy files are governed by the legacy repo's own gates, and its baseline file set is now read directly from git by legacy-change-accounting.

guards.name: multi-worker-overlap
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: multi-worker-overlap.

guards.name: no-positional-identity
guards.invariant: No durable identity is positional or borrowed: every run, worker, workflow, node, gate, actor, delegation-edge, and extracted-record id rejects an index, an ordinal, and a stringified number, and a UUID cannot be spelled as any slug-shaped id, so a run id can never stand in as a worker id.

guards.name: notification-durability
guards.invariant: D137 (doc 03 §2.6/§10.4 D79b; doc 12 §6): a notification is a durable record FIRST and a desktop delivery second. `publish` settles create-or-fold in one authority transaction and only then attempts OS delivery, and the load-bearing arm injects a delivery that throws — the item must still be durably unread with its count and version untouched, because the operator who missed the toast has only the inbox left. No per-attempt delivery state is written. Each of doc 03 §2.6's closed triggers commits an item and routes to its ratified D79b channel (failed/gate-waiting/write-parked/repeating/storage → ping, verified-done → inbox), each carries its own dedupe identity that excludes the occurrence, and a repeat FOLDS into the one (actorId, dedupeFingerprint) row — count up, lastSeenAt advanced, unread again — rather than minting a second. Snooze suppresses delivery only and never flips status; read state and snooze move independently; a stale version is refused. The trigger event union is ids, closed codes, and counts, so notification text has no free-text channel a captured value could enter through.

guards.name: one-projection-counts
guards.invariant: D81 (doc 03 §10.1): there is exactly ONE server-side run/queue projection and every dashboard count descends from its payload. Structurally, the count fields (monthCounts/workflowCounts/statusCounts) are constructed in exactly one production module — src/server/dashboard/projectors/run-queue-projection.ts — and nowhere else in src/, so a second aggregate endpoint or a client-side re-derivation fails by file name. A seeded world with hidden, delegated (operation+member), rejected/failed, gated, and terminal rows proves Workflow Panel total == Status Bar sum == rendered Queue Panel row count by construction, with containment and hiding applied once inside the projection. Archived rows join the fixture when the D80 archive service lands (2i).

guards.name: one-time-import-offline
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: one-time-import-offline.

guards.name: permanent-key-dedupe
guards.invariant: A strict system-scoped natural idempotency key and its derived digest identify one permanent SQLite intent across sequential and independent competing connections; committed and observed-present rows cannot be reopened, observed-present creates no attempt or write ledger/span outbox, and any key/digest mismatch fails loud.

guards.name: ucpath-person-org-strict
guards.invariant: The UCPath Person Organizational Summary runtime pins exact legacy provenance while rejecting body-name scans, observed-EID overwrite, extraction-error empty defaults, missing-grid not-found inference, swallowed clears, and drill-null fallbacks; search results expand before extraction and again after Return to Search, Employment Instances expand before assignment selection, enabled View All must transition to View N while disabled View All alone proves already-complete, contextual one-to-many selector ports remain closed and unique, every operation locator resolves through dual evidence, and both subject proofs fail loud. The locator-coverage arm is scoped to the two Person Org SCREENS in both directions (D130 added a second UCPath screen family), and the SS Smart HR receipt elements are asserted present and unreachable from this operation so the scoping can never go vacuous.

guards.name: preflight-coverage
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: preflight-coverage.

guards.name: provider-capability-boundary
guards.invariant: Every capability maps exactly once to a strict immutable provider budget and reaches remote I/O only through the single durable admission kernel; whole-src and transitive task import scans confine raw network/vendor modules and adapters to infra/providers, forbid hidden ProviderClient construction, prove exhaustion makes zero adapter calls/non-sleep requeue, and keep Phase-1f provider modules deterministic with production pools/consumers absent until Phase 2h.

guards.name: rebuild-gates
guards.invariant: D93: the absent-tree / present-but-empty temp_src activation dance retires with temp_src. This repo's roots exist from its first commit; gate-coverage pins the plain script family and guard-manifest still proves every active arm resolves a non-empty file set.

guards.name: recovery-negative-proof-settlement
guards.invariant: Retry authority requires the exact configured number of schema-valid post-window observations at or beyond both injected-Clock timing boundaries, all bound to the fenced key and exact authoritative query/source/source-state; early, single, malformed, future, inconsistent, wrong-boundary, ambiguous, unknown, present, and operator-only evidence never becomes retryable.

guards.name: runtime-isolation
guards.invariant: D93: two repositories share no module graph, so the cross-tree bridge scan proves an impossibility. The configuration half — distinct commands, state/artifact roots, ports, process locks, and browser profiles on one machine — survives in operational-isolation.

guards.name: scenario-coverage
guards.invariant: Every branch arm, gate open/resolve, delegation size/replay/policy, and transaction outcome derived from the node tuple is claimed by a registered scenario, and every claim resolves to a path that still exists — so a renamed arm cannot keep a deleted path looking covered.

guards.name: semantic-ui-registry
guards.invariant: Every server-private semantic UI definition has a globally unique classified id, collision-free search intent, resolved same-system/same-screen acyclic dependencies, non-vacuous globally unique verification scenarios, exact dual sanitized evidence-to-screen/scenario/date/port-row bindings, and byte-fresh recipe-free generated catalogs; disjoint legacy candidate ids cannot enter any runtime catalog kind. The guarded projection set is DERIVED, never enumerated: it equals the set of stores shipping a `driver/ui-registry.ts` in both directions (no unguarded publisher, no orphan UI-CATALOG.md), so a newly added store's markdown cannot escape freshness enforcement the way `src/stores/kuali/UI-CATALOG.md` did. Every derived projection — the JSON and each per-system markdown — carries stale and missing negative controls through an injected reader.

guards.name: single-flight-login
guards.invariant: Session login is single-flight within one worker/system session creation (doc 05 §4): store.session.login is invoked only inside the worker session manager, and two concurrent leases for one system produce exactly one session open and one authentication.

guards.name: sleep-budget
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: sleep-budget.

guards.name: storage-recovery
guards.invariant: Native online backups self-verify the completed copy, bind immutable manifests to final bytes, coalesce generation-follow-up work, fail closed into read-only degraded authority, keep doctor read-only, and permit only stopped-proof offline restore from an exact verified compatible backup without exposing DatabaseSync or using live-WAL copy/VACUUM fallbacks.

guards.name: subject-before-fence
guards.invariant: Every transaction pairs compatible prepare/commit subject declarations observed after prepare in one system; the live sequencer orders prepare-end < fresh subject observation < fence-commit < mutation-call on one lease; mismatch/unknown/missing observation produces zero fence and zero click with a poisoned page; alternating EIDs through one pooled page bind distinct digests; every minted MutationCapability is bound to the exact fenced WriteBindingProof digest and is refused by the production Kuali driver when it was not sequencer-minted; unscoped commits require a reviewed allowlisted reason, fail-both-ways.

guards.name: task-contract-sealing
guards.invariant: Read, prepare, and commit contracts are minted only by the validating deep-seal factory; the exact effect-discriminated runtime definition rejects unknown/effect-only fields, empty error-code lists, and non-memory prepare checkpoints; recursive schemas reject nested open/any/unknown/record escapes; parsed canonical examples and closed write-safety proofs agree; unscoped commits require reviewed reason ids; schema-owned paths/tiers/references fail loud; inferred error codes stay literal; and an AST plus transitive import graph protects every src/**/contracts/** module from runtime imports, forged seals, casts, and dynamic-import bypasses.

guards.name: task-driver-boundary
guards.invariant: AST and transitive import-graph audits confine static/dynamic Playwright access, raw browser types, locator/frame/getBy/newPage/evaluate/$ operations, and private driver/session ownership to the two raw-browser owner families — per-system driver/session modules and the `src/infra/browser/**` worker session factory that owns concrete browser creation; task/workflow code consumes typed semantic ids and proofs and may reach neither family transitively. MutationCapability may be conjured by `as`/`satisfies` nowhere outside `src/base/mutation-capability.ts`, `mintMutationCapability` has exactly one permitted caller (`src/core/write-sequencer.ts`), and a `commit` implementation is legal only inside a `src/stores/<system>/driver/**` owner that validates its capability before clicking (D122).

guards.name: task-store-boundaries
guards.invariant: All nine closed browser systems have exactly one declared store and fail-loud unwired session provider; driver/session/store systems match, OnBase alone is identity-exclusive, typed task bindings enforce effect/access/session/provider boundaries, and the registry exact-matches implementations to the contract corpus while resolving every scenario/probe/verifier reference.

guards.name: transaction-pairing
guards.invariant: A transaction pairs prepare and commit arms from one system under one lease, binds the commit key from workflow input and declared upstream outputs only, declares a positive probe-to-fence budget and a dry-run policy, carries a same-system read probe, and no commit contract is reachable as a standalone step anywhere in src/.

guards.name: worker-teardown-soak
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: worker-teardown-soak.

guards.name: workflow-editor-compile-integrity
guards.invariant: Planned Phase 1+ guard: workflow-editor-compile-integrity.

guards.name: write-safety-contract
guards.invariant: Every effect:commit contract declares complete write safety with no escape hatch: nontrivial proofSchema, normal-output/present-probe extractors, outputFromProof reconstruction, and a same-store read probe; the completion union admits receipt AND save-verify/upload-verify without a confirmation number; and doc 09 SS4 recovery routes probe-first with present proof schema-validated before backfill, single early absence yielding zero retry authority, only D64/D69 stabilized evidence settling retryable, indeterminate arms parking, and the permanent key blocking every second fence.

guards.name: authentication-proof-not-url
guards.invariant: Doc 05 §4: a browser session's authentication is never concluded from a URL. Every store login recipe is built by defineVerifiedLoginRecipe so its content-level proof runs on EVERY return path, no recipe produces a LoginResult outside that wrapper, every landed BrowserSystemBinding supplies a verifier rather than an isAuthenticatedUrl predicate, and the factory's neutral reset asserts through assertAuthenticatedApplication.
